# `get_setting`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read the full device settings object.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xf23c0, GetSetting @0xea600 (64-bit build); firmware 9.75 request member from the 9.75 reports |

No request parameters are read; the getter always formats the full settings, never a filtered subset (a filter belongs to Setting events). Member presence depends on process type, camera, capabilities and helper success; failed sub-queries omit their members and the reply stays a success. In process type 1 the settings of the peer camera are included under second_camera, via a sequential 10,000 ms peer wait. The serialized object repeats beep_volume and ae_bri_percent and may repeat effect_offset_deg; see the result schema. Several members are absent on the 32-bit build. Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0: params may carry include_sensitive (boolean or integer, default true); false omits the password member, and the flag is forwarded to the second camera. Firmware 9.75 members: annotation (object), sky_replay (always false), can_encrypt (constant true), comet_max_frame_num (constant 200), enable_dark_library, motion_monitor (object, 64-bit build), preview.raw_bin2, exp_ms.more_exposure, and for the wide camera stack.startrails_duration_min and stack.startrail_mode; the main-process, full-path-only and wide-camera gates are on the result schema. expert_mode is still emitted. comet_max_frame_num is the comet batch input frame limit (output only); startrail_mode 0, 1, 2 select the maximum video, the decay video or both, and startrails_duration_min is in minutes (-1 or 0 no limit). Firmware 9.31: no request member is read.

Side effects: Refreshes shared camera info, reads GPIO heater state, network configuration and the connection password, runs the Alpaca status script and queries the peer camera; conditional slave-storage synchronisation. No setting is written. The tier is C because of live driver queries, though the call is routinely used as a read. Asynchronous events: unresolved.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_setting"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Firmware 9.31: not read; omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Firmware 9.75: an object with the optional include_sensitive; clients SHOULD omit params otherwise. [READ] |
| `params.include_sensitive` | boolean\|integer | no | true | Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0: parsed as boolean or integer (nonzero is true); a failed parse is ignored and the default stays. False omits the password setting. Forwarded to the second camera. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

No handler-level error branch. Dynamic downstream failures omit members instead of producing errors. There is no error 123 (a loaded byte 0x7b is the JSON opening brace).

## Example

Request, request - No parameters:

```json
{"id":141,"method":"get_setting"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_setting","result":{"temp_unit":"C","lang":"en","guest_mode":false,"dark_mode":true,"wide_cam":false,"stack":{"dbe":false,"light_duration_min":10,"brightness":0.0,"contrast":0.0,"saturation":0.0,"dbe_enable":false},"ae_bri_percent":50.0},"code":0,"id":141}
```
